chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: Atlantic City 1915 and breaking the gambling habit
summary: Wooding recalls going to Atlantic City with an entertainer, Charley Johnson teaching him to gamble, and his quitting after a Sunday morning.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, this was around the latter part of 1915. And I was just in the practice of being a pianist. I didn't know how it was going to turn out because I was really lost. I'd dropped out of high school and now I was trying to make it on my own because I was going against the wishes of my parents.
Uh hunh. So what did you -- you were living by yourself then.

I'd gone to Atlantic City with a lady that was an entertainer. And she was older than I was and she was trying to run things like she wanted. She said, 'Well, here I got my stooge and I'll take him on with me and we'll have a good time together. And when I get tired, I'll toss him off.' But, in the meantime, I met two or three fellows down there. Especially one, Charley Johnson, that was a great help to me and showed me the ropes and how to go about it, and all. So, he showed me how to do a lot of things. In fact, he taught me how to gamble. And every Saturday night we both would get
broke in the place. Because these fellows were waiting for us. Well, we come in.

So, one Sunday morning I was standing on the corner eating a ten cent can of salmon. Which the same salmon nowadays costs around $2.50. It was ten cents then, see? And I said, "Look here, Charley. I'm tired of standing around on the road getting broke ever time." I had a little job. I was working at a little place called the Bucket of Blood. And I wasn't making much, and half that was going, a lot of times, in tabs for my friends coming in there. So I said, "Charley, I'm going to stop gambling. If I've got any money to waste, I'm going to spend it on these chicks around here." "Cause", I said, "I don't have no fun just taking my money that's in my hand, it's the only time about an hour and a half, and then the other fellow's got it." So, I was through. That's the last time I gambled. But Charley went on gambling and didn't come out to no good for him. You see, so that's one habit I broke up.
